brief:
# Build: headless-tabs (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now.

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `headless-tabs`, branch claude/headless-tabs) with the steps below + in-progress banner entry, per standing rules. Check the pending queue.
- Builds `orch-live-sync` and `notes-vault` are running in parallel and touch the builds store / claude-sync: never hand-edit store.json, go through the orchestrator CLI. If orch-live-sync's live status writes (framework/cli/builds-live.mjs) are on main by the time you finish a step, use them.

## What Brett wants
1. Every terminal tab in the console's terminal (the Windows Terminal plugin / terminal in the console) runs on a session that never dies, like Mosh/Moshi: it survives disconnects, reloads, phone sleep, and stays current. Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). Closing a tab detaches, it doesn't kill (explicit "Kill session" with confirm).
2. Every time a headless session starts (deploy/claude-headless.sh, `vps.build_start`, agent swarm jobs, orchestrator-launched builds), the console automatically opens a NEW tab attached to that build's tmux session (axf-<name>). Works for builds started while the console is closed too: on open, tabs for all running headless sessions appear.
3. Tab title bar: the agent running it (agent/persona name from the session's env/brief/swarm roster, e.g. the swarm agent name, else the build name) + model + a real-time cost counter that climbs as it spends. Cost: run claude -p with `--output-format stream-json --verbose` (or tee it alongside the human log) and sum usage per message (input, output, cache read, cache write) x the model's price table (config file, not hard-coded in UI); final value reconciles to the result event's total_cost_usd. Expose cost via a small server route/websocket so the title updates live. Show status dot (working / waiting / done / failed).
4. The tab splits into two panes; split direction vertical or horizontal (toggle in the tab menu + default in Settings, remembered per tab). Pane A = the live session. Pane B = the context chain: as the session reads CLAUDE.md and every file it pulls in (imports/@ references, .claude/rules, _claude/rules/RULES.md, shared rules, instructions, persona, memory, THREADS etc.), show the chain as a tree in the order it happens, and print the rules it picks up ONE AT A TIME, deliberately slower than real time (typewriter/reveal pacing, speed setting, skip-to-end button), so Brett can watch what the agent is learning. Source the chain from the session's actual reads (stream-json tool events for Read, plus the CLAUDE.md load order Claude Code uses); rules = the bullet/heading items of each file.
5. Tokens only, follows the hub look, phone-friendly (on narrow screens the split stacks and becomes swipeable).

## Steps
- s1 Persistent tmux-backed tabs + reconnect/resume in the console terminal; Moshi attach command; detach vs kill.
- s2 Headless launcher emits session-start events (claude-headless.sh + build_start path + swarm/orchestrator launches) with build name, agent, model, tmux session; console auto-opens tabs, and lists running ones on load.
- s3 stream-json capture alongside the human log; cost meter service (price table config) + live route.
- s4 Tab title: agent, model, live cost, status dot.
- s5 Split pane with vertical/horizontal toggle + setting.
- s6 Context chain pane: tree in read order + slow rule-by-rule reveal, speed setting, skip.
- s7 Help pack, tests, check-theme/check-controls, lifecycle, UI Review shots, report `_claude/builds/reports/headless-tabs.md`, THREADS.md, PR.
Mark each step done through the store as you finish it. Android port: log as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - where it goes
Everything in this build goes INTO the console's existing built-in Terminal plugin (Terminal v0.3.0: frameless window, tab strip as title bar, connections, profiles, Windows keys; window engine resize/snap/maximize from refactor-all s17-s23, see `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/windows-terminal.md` and `windows-terminal-fable.md`). Extend that plugin; do NOT create a separate terminal plugin or a second terminal UI. Persistent tmux sessions become the Terminal's session backend / a connection type, auto-opened headless tabs are Terminal tabs, title/cost/status live in its tab strip, the split + context-chain pane are Terminal pane features. Bump the Terminal plugin version and keep every existing feature working.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - clarification, overrides any ambiguity above
Target = the Terminal PLUGIN produced by the Refactor build `windows-terminal` (the Windows-Terminal-style plugin, v0.3.0, in the console's plugins folder). NOT any terminal hardwired into the console core/shell. If the console core has its own built-in terminal, leave it untouched. All features of this build (persistent tmux/Moshi sessions, auto headless tabs, agent name + live cost + status in the tab strip, vertical/horizontal split, context-chain pane) live inside that plugin. If you already started any of it outside the plugin, move it into the plugin.

## ADDENDUM 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - Tooltip mode (add as step s8)
- Terminal plugin Settings gets a switch **Tooltip mode** (off by default, saved in terminal-settings@1, carries data-axf-level, help text).
- When on: the FIRST tap/click on any command-toolbar item does NOT run it; it shows a tooltip saying what the button does (reuse the existing help pack text for that control; every toolbar item must have one) and the button stays lit (highlighted/armed state via tokens) for 3 seconds with a subtle countdown. A SECOND tap on the same button within those 3 seconds runs it. After 3 s, or tapping elsewhere/another button, it disarms (tapping another button arms that one instead). Keyboard shortcuts are unaffected. Works on touch and mouse; the tooltip stays on screen on phones (not hover-only). Make the 3 s a setting (default 3).
- Tests for arm/run/timeout/switch, UI Review shots of the armed state on phone + desktop.

uiReview.name: Headless tabs: agent, model, live cost, split with the context chain

open: Interactive (non-headless) Claude Code tabs have no cost meter or context chain: they don't speak stream-json. Their transcript could feed the same meter later.

The `events.jsonl` log is written but the console reads the live list from `tmux ls` (tags included), which already covers sessions started while the console was closed; the log is there for other readers (Build manager, axHub).
The console's local tmux tabs end when the console container is rebuilt (VPS tabs do not).
